alex: Quick heads-up — ran a focused kernel + batching sweep on the 1B PP+TP config this morning; results are noisy but reproducible.
jin: summary: throughput dropped ~18% when activation checkpointing (remat) crosses the PP boundary; observed all-reduce latency spikes up to 3.2x during recompute windows.
alex: ouch. did you isolate KV cache behavior? iirc that can amplify stalls.
jin: yes — TTL and kv metrics show eviction spikes (~15%) right at recompute start. small sequence lengths make it worse.
sam: can you paste the profile snippet?
jin: ```
PROFILE SNAPSHOT (step 120..160):
- avg_token_ms: baseline 12.1ms -> remat 14.3ms (+18%)
- allreduce_time_pct: baseline 9% -> remat-window 28%
- kernel_launch_count: +22% (many small-launches)
- memcpy stalls (cpu->gpu): 2% -> 6%
- kvcache_miss_rate: 0.8% -> 12% (spike during recompute replay)
```
rita: that's a big signal. are we switching kernel paths during replay? fallback to safer kernels maybe?
jin: yes — kernel router flips to a "safe" small-kernel path for fused q/k/v ops when seq len / mem pattern changes; that increases launch overhead.
kevin: batching heuristic note: when remat triggers extra compute, the effective microbatch per-device drops. our continuous-batching window currently flushes earlier -> less compute to overlap with allreduce.
alex: so: remat -> replay compute -> kvcache churn -> smaller microbatches -> more frequent allreduces with poor compute overlap -> latency surge.
sam: any quick mitigations we can try on prod or a canary?
jin: tried increasing batch-fill delay to 30ms: reduced allreduce frequency ~40% but added median tail +2ms. also tried pinning kernel routing hint to prefer larger fused kernels and that cut launch overhead ~15%.
rita: sounds promising. i'd prefer a remat-aware batching rule: when remat is detected, favor larger batch windows and prefer allreduce fusion for small tensors.
kevin: another observation: switching to the int8 attention kernel path prevented the router flip in our tests and reduced small-kernel launches. quant path seems more stable wrt seq len jitter.
alex: can we gate this behind a config flag? e.g., `prefer_large_kernel=true` when remat_flag set?
jin: i'll prototype a small patch to batching logic + kernel routing hint: if remat_flag && pp_crossing then set prefer_large_kernel=true and bump batch_fill_ms to 30.
sam: :thumbsup: keep it small and measurable. add tracepoints for kvcache hit/miss around remat windows so we have guardrails.
rita: noted. let's plan a canary on the dedicated 4-GPU pool tomorrow, measure allreduce_time_pct and kvcache_miss_rate.
perf-bot: created perf-test job `remat-pp-allreduce-check` (ref 9832) — scheduled nightly.
jin: i'll attach the prototype and profiling traces to the issue.
sam: also add a simple CI perf check that runs a short remat+pp scenario and ensures allreduce_time_pct doesn't regress >5% vs baseline.
alex: good call. please file the issue with steps + metrics to watch and link the perf job. thanks everyone.
rita: thanks — will own canary coordination.
kevin: if the canary looks good we can ship the batching hint as a fallback only for models with frequent remat-triggered kv churn.
alex: filing issue now and adding next steps in the ticket.
